symbols.name: k
symbols.def: number of distinct queried treatment levels

symbols.name: s^\star
symbols.role: queried outcome label for each queried treatment; repetitions are allowed

symbols.name: q
symbols.role: generic finite response law for \(X,\mathbf Y\)

symbols.name: Q
symbols.role: generic endpoint-attaining response law used in the support frontier

symbols.name: g
symbols.role: mass not forced to fail by factual consistency

symbols.name: W
symbols.role: maximum value of the deleted-diagonal failure flow

symbols.name: c_{(\cdot)}
symbols.def: \(c_{(1)}\leq\cdots\leq c_{(k)}\) is the nondecreasing rearrangement of \(c_1,\ldots,c_k\)

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: total binary encoding length of rational \(o\) and \(e\)

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: least common multiple of denominators of rational \(o\) and \(e\)

symbols.name: \operatorname{TAKE}
symbols.role: selects mass \(w\) from a finite eligible union \(E\) while introducing at most one new cell boundary

symbols.name: \mathcal C_N
symbols.def: compatible probability tables within the blockwise \(\varepsilon\)-boxes around \(\widehat o,\widehat e\)
symbols.role: finite-sample confidence region for the margins

symbols.name: I_N
symbols.def: \(I_N=[\min_{(o',e')\in\mathcal C_N}L(o',e'),\max_{(o',e')\in\mathcal C_N}U(o',e')]\) when \(\mathcal C_N\neq\varnothing\), and \(I_N=[0,1]\) otherwise

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{m,r,k}
symbols.def: For \(2\leq k\leq m\), \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}=\{(o,e)\in\Delta(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y)\times\Delta(\mathcal Y)^m:e_{is}\geq o_{is}\text{ for every }i\in\mathcal X,s\in\mathcal Y\}=\{(o,e):\mathcal Q(o,e)\neq\varnothing\}\).

symbols.name: s_L
symbols.role: minimum support size among lower-endpoint laws

symbols.name: s_U
symbols.role: minimum support size among upper-endpoint laws

symbols.name: s_\star
symbols.role: worst-case frontier of the two separate endpoint support minima

assumptions.condition: \(e_{is}\geq o_{is}\) for every \(i\in\mathcal X\) and \(s\in\mathcal Y\).
Under \(q\), \(\Pr_q(X=i,Y_i=s)=o_{is}\) for every \(i\in\mathcal X\) and \(s\in\mathcal Y\).
Under \(q\), \(\Pr_q(Y_j=s)=e_{js}\) for every \(j\in\mathcal X\) and \(s\in\mathcal Y\).
The observational block contains \(n_0\) independent draws from the categorical law \(o\).
For each \(j\in\mathcal X\), intervention block \(j\) contains \(n_j\) independent draws from the categorical law \(e_{j,\cdot}\).

definitions.name: Compatible response-law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Q(o,e)=\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y^m):Y=Y_X\ q\text{-a.s.},\ \Pr_q(X=i,Y_i=s)=o_{is},\ \Pr_q(Y_j=s)=e_{js}\text{ for all }i,j\in\mathcal X,s\in\mathcal Y\}\).

definitions.name: Indicator-coarsened margins
definitions.construction: For \(j\in\mathcal J\), set \(A_j=\{Y_j=s_j^\star\}\), \(p_i=\sum_{s\in\mathcal Y}o_{is}\), \(a_j=e_{j,s_j^\star}\), \(b_j=o_{j,s_j^\star}\), \(c_j=a_j-b_j\), \(d_j=p_j-b_j\), \(h_j=1-p_j-c_j\), \(p_0=1-\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j\), \(g=p_0+\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}b_j\), and \(H=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}h_j\).

definitions.name: Closed scalar endpoint maps
definitions.construction: \(L(o,e)=\max\{0,\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}a_j-k+1,\max_{i\in\mathcal J}(b_i-\sum_{j\in\mathcal J\setminus\{i\}}h_j)\}\) and \(U(o,e)=\min\{g,\min_{j\in\mathcal J}a_j,\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal J,|S|\geq2}(\sum_{j\in S}c_j)/(|S|-1)\}\).

definitions.name: Finite-cell TAKE refinement
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{TAKE}(E,w)\) traverses a finite ordered partition of an eligible set \(E\), consumes whole cells until mass \(w\) is reached, and splits at most the final consumed cell; \(w=0\) returns the empty selection and no split.

definitions.name: Intersection-packing construction
definitions.construction: At \(t=U(o,e)\), initialize \(t_i=(t-c_i)_+\), enlarge \(t_i\leq b_i\) and \(t_0\leq p_0\) until \(t_0+\sum_{i\in\mathcal J}t_i=t\), place a common event of mass \(t_i\) in each factual-success block and mass \(t_0\) in the unqueried block, then fill coordinate \(i\)'s remaining success demand outside its own stratum by \(\operatorname{TAKE}\).

definitions.name: Deleted-diagonal failure flow
definitions.construction: Build a network with source arcs of capacity \(h_j\) to left nodes \(j\in\mathcal J\), middle arcs of capacity \(2\) from \(j\) to right nodes \(i\in\{0\}\cup\mathcal J\) only when \(i\neq j\), right capacities \(p_0\) at node \(0\) and \(b_i\) at node \(i\in\mathcal J\), and use \(\operatorname{TAKE}\) to realize a maximum flow as disjoint failure pieces before filling every residual row demand inside the already covered failure union.

definitions.name: Block-multinomial confidence polytope
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_N\) is the set of \(o',e'\) satisfying the probability-simplex and cell-compatibility restrictions together with \(|o'_{is}-\widehat o_{is}|\leq\varepsilon_0\) and \(|e'_{js}-\widehat e_{js}|\leq\varepsilon_j\) for all cells.

definitions.name: Endpoint confidence-region inversion
definitions.construction: If \(\mathcal C_N\neq\varnothing\), set \(I_N=[\min_{(o',e')\in\mathcal C_N}L(o',e'),\max_{(o',e')\in\mathcal C_N}U(o',e')]\); otherwise set \(I_N=[0,1]\). Represent the lower optimization with one epigraph variable and the upper optimization with variables \(z_j\geq0\), \(z_j\geq t-c_j\), and \(\sum_jz_j\leq t\).

definitions.name: Cycle-cancellation support handle
definitions.construction: For the uniform upper direction, apply cycle cancellation separately to the lower- and upper-endpoint transportation tables, then compress within each categorical block of the finite-cell \(\operatorname{TAKE}\) refinement while retaining the active affine or minimum-cut certificate. For the matching lower direction, use endpoint-face rank and forced-positive-cell obstructions to construct compatible margin families for which \(\max\{s_L(o,e),s_U(o,e)\}\) is large.

statements.statement: Under the two simplex restrictions, \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\neq\varnothing\) if and only if \(e_{is}\geq o_{is}\) for every \(i\in\mathcal X\) and \(s\in\mathcal Y\).
statements.justification: This isolates the complete observable feasibility condition and rules out hidden cross-coordinate restrictions before sharpness is studied.
statements.gap: Shu--Wang--Li use the same consistency-implied cell inequalities, but the categorical sufficiency construction is not their all-dimensional sharpness theorem.
statements.consumer: A researcher can reject incoherent observational and intervention margins before evaluating any conjunction bound.

statements.statement: Every finite law of \(X\) and \((\mathbf 1\{A_j\})_{j\in\mathcal J}\) satisfying \(\Pr(X=i)=p_i\), \(\Pr(A_j)=a_j\), and \(\Pr(X=j,A_j)=b_j\) admits a finite refinement in \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\) that preserves all indicator atoms and hence preserves \(\theta\). The refinement uses \(\operatorname{TAKE}\) separately inside and outside each factual stratum, including zero-mass domains, and the refined law is realized by an SCM with one finite exogenous variable.
statements.justification: The exact coarsening converse is what transfers a binary indicator completion back to every categorical observational and interventional cell.
statements.gap: Neither the scalar validity proof of Shu--Wang--Li nor the binary response-table construction of Xie--Li establishes this all-alphabet refinement lemma.
statements.consumer: Any future sharp binary-event coupling result can be lifted to multivalued PoC margins without enumerating categorical response signatures.

statements.statement: The intersection-packing construction returns a member of \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\) with \(\theta=U(o,e)\). Moreover, \(\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}(t-c_j)_+\leq t\) is equivalent to \((|S|-1)t\leq\sum_{j\in S}c_j\) for every \(S\subseteq\mathcal J\) with \(|S|\geq2\), so an active subset is a dual certificate.
statements.justification: This proves universal attainability of every possible active upper affine piece without enumerating subsets or response types.
statements.gap: Shu--Wang--Li prove upper validity and selected equality regimes; their paper leaves the every-input all-dimensional construction open.
statements.consumer: A PoC analyst receives an explicit witness law and a short active-affine certificate for the largest feasible conjunction probability.

statements.statement: The deleted-diagonal network has maximum value \(W(o,e)=\min\{H,g,\min_{i\in\mathcal J}(H-h_i+g-b_i)\}\). Its realized flow and residual-failure filling return a member of \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\) with \(\theta=g-W(o,e)=L(o,e)\); whenever a left row has positive unused capacity, every adjacent right block is saturated, so its remaining demand can be filled inside the existing failure union.
statements.justification: The saturation implication is the nonnegative residual invariant that closes the lower endpoint for every compatible margin vector.
statements.gap: Xie--Li solve the binary response system by finite active regions; Koperberg supplies Hall machinery but not this PoC-specific diagonal deletion and residual categorical completion.
statements.consumer: The min-cut identity provides a checkable explanation of which factual stratum or total failure capacity determines the sharp lower probability.

statements.statement: For every compatible real input with arbitrary finite \(m\) and \(r\), distinct queried treatments \(2\leq k\leq m\), and arbitrary possibly repeated labels \(s^\star\), the identified set \(\{\theta(q):q\in\mathcal Q(o,e)\}\) equals the full interval \([L(o,e),U(o,e)]\). Both endpoints are attained by finite SCM laws, and convex mixtures of two endpoint laws attain every interior value. These endpoints are exactly the Shu--Wang--Li Theorem 2 scalar formulas after unequal-alphabet padding and label replaceability.
statements.justification: This is the missing all-dimensional pointwise sharpness theorem for the published scalar conjunction bounds.
statements.gap: Shu--Wang--Li prove soundness and low-dimensional computational tightness, while Xie--Li prove every-input attainment only for binary PNS.
statements.consumer: A customer-journey analyst with common-population observational choices and arm-specific intervention outcomes can interpret the scalar interval as the exact range for a prespecified cross-channel response pattern.

statements.statement: For rational input of total encoding length \(B\), compatibility and the endpoints are evaluable in \(O(mr+k\log k)\) arithmetic and comparison operations using \(c_{(\cdot)}\). Endpoint-attaining laws with support at most \(N_\star\), atom denominators dividing \(D\) for the lower endpoint and dividing \(D(\ell-1)\) for an upper endpoint certified by an active subset of size \(\ell\), and active-affine or minimum-cut optimality certificates are constructible and checkable in time polynomial in \(m,r,k,B\). Zero cells cause no division.
statements.justification: Sparse exact primal laws and short dual cuts turn a sharpness theorem into an auditable computational result.
statements.gap: Generic response-signature linear programs are sharp but can be exponentially represented and do not supply this structured endpoint evaluator or certificate size bound.
statements.consumer: A regulator or replication archive can verify every supplied categorical margin and endpoint using exact arithmetic without trusting a black-box exponential linear program.

statements.statement: Under block-multinomial sampling, \(\inf_{(o,e)}\Pr_{o,e}([L(o,e),U(o,e)]\subseteq I_N)\geq1-\alpha\), uniformly over all compatible margins, including zero cells, interval collapse, and arbitrary active-term ties. Both endpoints of \(I_N\) are solutions of rational linear programs with \(O(mr+k)\) variables and constraints when the radii are rationally rounded outward.
statements.justification: Confidence-region containment avoids differentiability and singular-covariance failures at active-set ties and simplex faces.
statements.gap: Cheng--Mao--Pearl--Li derive asymptotic regular and directional limits; generic partial-identification inference does not state this exact polynomial block-multinomial inversion.
statements.consumer: An applied analyst can report a finite-sample outer confidence interval for the entire sharp PoC interval even with rare or unobserved categorical cells.

statements.statement: The endpoint-attainment theorem makes both minimizing sets defining \(s_L(o,e)\) and \(s_U(o,e)\) nonempty on \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\). Determine the exact asymptotic order of \(s_\star(m,r,k)\). For the upper direction, establish one uniform order bound that controls both \(s_L(o,e)\) and \(s_U(o,e)\) for every \((o,e)\in\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\). For the lower direction, construct compatible margin families for which \(\max\{s_L(o,e),s_U(o,e)\}\), with the two minima taken separately, has the matching order. In particular, decide whether the quadratic \(k^2\) term in \(N_\star\) is intrinsic or removable uniformly over \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\).
statements.justification: The current polynomial support certificate is sufficient for computation but does not characterize the intrinsic complexity of exact causal witnesses.
statements.gap: Xie--Li give fixed binary response tables and generic linear programming gives broad basic-feasible-solution bounds; neither provides a matched structured support frontier as alphabets grow.
statements.consumer: A certificate standard for large categorical PoC audits needs the smallest worst-case witness format rather than a merely polynomial one.

sampling_model.design: One observational block and one block for each single-treatment intervention; each block is multinomial on its stated finite alphabet.
sampling_model.units: The observational block has \(n_0\) independent common-population units and intervention block \(j\) has \(n_j\) independent common-population units; cross-block independence is not required for the union-bound coverage statement.
sampling_model.treatment: The observational treatment is factual, while block \(j\) records outcomes under the intervention \(X\leftarrow j\).
sampling_model.overlap: No positive-cell condition is imposed; zero observational and intervention cells are allowed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance functions are estimated; empirical multinomial cell frequencies enter the confidence polytope.

estimand_functional: \(\theta\in[L(o,e),U(o,e)]\), with \(L=\max\{0,\sum_j a_j-k+1,\max_i(b_i-\sum_{j\neq i}h_j)\}\) and \(U=\min\{g,\min_j a_j,\min_{|S|\geq2}\sum_{j\in S}c_j/(|S|-1)\}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: A complete proof establishing their tightness remains open.
Deriving theoretically sharp bounds on the probabilities of causation.
The bounds of PNS given by Equations 4 and 5 are tight.
There exists an SCM such that the query coincides with the solution of the LP.
We define and provide theoretical bounds for all types of probabilities of causation with multivalued treatments and effects.
The limiting distribution is a minimum or maximum of finitely many correlated Gaussian linear forms.
Our theory provides finite-sample lower bounds on the coverage probabilities of the confidence intervals.

tldr: Common-population observational and single-treatment intervention margins determine the exact identified interval for any finite-alphabet scalar conjunction probability of causation. The published Shu--Wang--Li endpoints are attained for every compatible real input: an information-preserving indicator coarsening lifts back to all categorical cells, intersection packing attains the upper endpoint, and a deleted-diagonal maximum flow with a residual-failure invariant attains the lower endpoint. Rational inputs admit sorted endpoint evaluation, sparse exact SCM witnesses, and short active-affine or minimum-cut certificates; block-multinomial confidence-region inversion adds uniform finite-sample coverage without appropriating the directional asymptotics of Cheng--Mao--Pearl--Li.

project_justification.gap: Shu--Wang--Li prove all-dimensional validity but leave pointwise tightness open, while Xie--Li's constructive proof is binary and generic response-signature programs conceal the scalar geometry in exponentially many response states.
project_justification.niche: The common-population scalar conjunction problem has a coupling structure in which factual failures delete diagonal edges and all unused row capacity can be filled inside a saturated failure union.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives the exact indicator lifting, the packing and flow endpoint laws, the min-cut and sorted duals, audited polynomial witness complexity, and a boundary-safe finite-sample inversion of the resulting sharp interval.

related_work: Shu--Wang--Li Theorem 2 supplies the scalar affine formulas and explicitly leaves their general-dimensional tightness unresolved. Xie--Li Theorem 3.2 supplies the closest constructive precedent by solving the binary eight-cell system. Koperberg Proposition 6 supplies the finite Hall--Strassen coupling principle adapted to the lower deleted-diagonal network. Tian--Pearl supplies the binary PNS interval used solely as an unnumbered algebraic sanity regression for the general formulas and witness constructions. Li--Pearl provides the earlier recursive multivalued bounds but is not treated as a direct theorem target. Rossetto--Antonucci gives a generic sharp response-signature linear program and SCM realization; it is the computational baseline, not a theorem claimed to be improved in general. Cheng--Mao--Pearl--Li gives the active-set directional limit theory, which is credited rather than relabeled. Horowitz--Lee, Stoye, and Kaido--Molinari--Stoye motivate confidence-region and projection inference, while the stated finite-sample result is specialized to the present block-multinomial polytope. Harinen and coauthors provide the hypothetical common-population customer-journey setting in which a prespecified multichannel response-pattern probability is a concrete scalar consumer.
technical_internal_limitation: Scalar sharpness does not imply simultaneous sharpness for several response patterns. Separately summing scalar endpoint values can therefore produce an unattainable policy utility. The confidence interval is a conservative outer inversion and carries no optimal-width claim. The support bound \(N_\star\) is polynomial but is not asserted to equal the exact frontier \(s_\star(m,r,k)\), which compares the two separately minimized endpoint supports.
honest_scope: The finite max-flow/min-cut theorem, multinomial concentration, and polynomial-time rational linear programming are standard inputs. The all-alphabet TAKE refinement, endpoint constructions, residual invariant, support and denominator audit, and interval equality remain to be proved. Unequal alphabets and repeated queried labels are covered, but factual-conditioned representative PoCs, incomplete subpopulations, mediator restrictions, population mismatch, and simultaneous vectors of conjunctions are outside the theorem. The Tian--Pearl binary reduction is an unnumbered sanity corollary and regression test, not a research-target theorem; the proof plan retains its algebraic verification by specializing the endpoint formulas and both witness constructions to the binary case. For \(k=1\), the target is the known marginal \(a_1\); for \(r=1\), the interval is \([1,1]\). The exact order of \(s_\star(m,r,k)\), defined through the separate lower- and upper-endpoint minima over \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\), remains open.

seed_details.title: Constructive all-alphabet sharpness of scalar conjunction probabilities of causation
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Opened arXiv:2505.15274v4 and read the Introduction, Theorem 2, Appendix A.1, and Conclusion. Theorem 2 proves the displayed affine inequalities, while the Introduction and Conclusion state that a complete all-dimensional tightness proof remains open.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Validity stops before the every-input construction of a nonnegative joint response law. The first changed step from the binary Xie--Li proof is replacement of its eight-cell active-region case split by a categorical indicator lifting and a diagonal-deleted flow whose residual demand can be filled without enlarging the failure union.
seed_details.destination_search: Searched the treatment--outcome alphabet and method pair using all-alphabet conjunction PNS, tightness, max-flow, forbidden-diagonal coupling, response signatures, and the anchor authors. The closest hits were the binary construction, finite Strassen coupling theory, and generic response-signature linear programs; none states the closed all-alphabet completion theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Rossetto--Antonucci because their sharp response-signature linear program already attains every counterfactual bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: That program certifies an exponentially represented optimum; it does not derive the Shu--Wang--Li scalar formula from the full categorical margins, give a uniform endpoint construction, or supply the sorted and cut certificates claimed here.

seed_details.title: Boundary-safe finite-sample inversion for affine-envelope PoC bounds
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Opened arXiv:2602.17070 and read the Introduction, Theorems 1--2, the multilevel discussion, and Conclusion. The paper derives regular and directional asymptotic laws, including correlated Gaussian extrema at ties, but does not give finite-sample uniform block-multinomial coverage.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step replaces a selected active gradient by simultaneous containment of every multinomial cell, followed by optimization of the endpoint maps over the resulting compatible polytope.
seed_details.destination_search: Searched block-multinomial PoC confidence inversion, zero-cell boundary coverage, affine-envelope ties, and finite-sample optimization inference. Horowitz--Lee, Stoye, and Kaido--Molinari--Stoye are adjacent but do not specialize a polynomial exact inversion to these PoC margins.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Horowitz--Lee by placing multinomial moments in their generic confidence region.
seed_details.rebuttal: Generic containment motivates the proof, but the polynomial positive-part inversion, exact boundary convention, and simultaneous coverage of the newly proved sharp PoC interval require the specialized affine and compatibility geometry.

seed_details.title: Sharpness frontier for substitute, replacement, and necessity representatives
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Opened arXiv:2505.15274v4 and read Theorems 3--5, the equivalence and replaceability results, their appendix proof boundaries, and Conclusion. The formulas are valid, but a universal construction for the additional factual treatment or outcome slices is not supplied.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is a sliced lifting that must preserve the factual event while allocating off-diagonal counterfactual labels; the scalar conjunction flow cannot simply be reused because its residual fills may cross the pinned factual slice.
seed_details.destination_search: Searched each representative name with multivalued sharpness, categorical flow, and factual-slice coupling. The binary tightness paper and partial-diagram programs were closest; no every-margin all-alphabet construction or obstruction frontier was located.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the scalar conjunction construction after intersecting with the observed treatment or outcome event.
seed_details.rebuttal: Intersection changes the available residual domains and can destroy the saturation invariant, so a new sliced feasibility theorem or a counterexample is required.

seed_details.title: Layered-flow sharp bounds under incomplete subpopulation margins
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Opened the R-29 paper and read its Introduction, binary bounding construction, discussion of incomplete and subpopulation regimes, and Conclusion. Its exact constructions are binary and it identifies the nonbinary response program as future work.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step replaces the binary observed-versus-missing decomposition by a layered categorical flow that allocates subgroup mass while retaining the query-specific forbidden coincidences.
seed_details.destination_search: Searched multivalued incomplete-subpopulation PoC with flow, transport, and response-law optimization. No compact nonbinary flow or necessary-and-sufficient informativeness frontier was found.
seed_details.red_team: A subgroup index is merely another outcome label, so the common-population theorem applies verbatim.
seed_details.rebuttal: Missing subgroup margins and population-specific sampling introduce unobserved mass-sharing constraints that are absent when every margin refers to one complete population.

seed_details.title: An if-and-only-if mediator coarsening frontier for convex PoC programs
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Opened arXiv:2602.14503 and read the Introduction, response-distribution program, mediator constraints, theorem statements, and Conclusion. Mediator restrictions generate bilinear equalities, whereas the tractable covariate cases remain linear.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to characterize when the mediator response table has a rank-one or separable parametrization whose projection onto the conjunction objective is convex and exact.
seed_details.destination_search: Searched mediator PoC convexification, bilinear response-function programs, exact coarsening, and nonnegative-rank conditions. No checkable if-and-only-if structural frontier for this PoC program was located.
seed_details.red_team: The proposed condition will either restate conditional independence or restrict to a trivial observed mediator.
seed_details.rebuttal: A viable theorem must prove both exact convexification and a boundary counterexample, but no defensible nontrivial condition was derived in this cold start.

seed_details.title: Sharp joint region for overlapping conjunction PoCs
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Opened the scalar representative results and the equivalence discussion in arXiv:2505.15274v4. The paper treats scalar queries, and no simultaneous attainability claim for several overlapping conjunctions appears in the theorem statements or Conclusion.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step replaces a single failure-cover flow by a coupled multiobjective transport or submodular-flow problem in which different scalar endpoints cannot be optimized independently.
seed_details.destination_search: Searched joint probabilities-of-causation region, overlapping conjunction counterfactual polytope, submodular flow, and simultaneous sharpness. Generic response-signature programs occupy computation but not a compact characterization.
seed_details.red_team: The joint set is just the projection of the generic response-signature polytope and therefore conceptually settled.
seed_details.rebuttal: Projection gives an exponential implicit set; a polynomial separation oracle or explicit nonrepresentability theorem would be new, but neither was yet derived.

seed_details.title: Critical-population-shift sensitivity for conjunction PoCs
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Opened R-29 and read its data-availability setup, binary subpopulation formulas, and Conclusion. It treats missing or subgroup information but does not parameterize violations of common-population comparability for multivalued conjunctions.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step augments the categorical coupling by a total-variation transport budget between observational and experimental populations, then dualizes that budget jointly with the deleted-diagonal cuts.
seed_details.destination_search: Searched PoC population transport sensitivity, total-variation common-population violation, and critical shift thresholds. No closed multivalued conjunction formula or sign-reversal threshold was located.
seed_details.red_team: A total-variation neighborhood only adds a generic Lipschitz enlargement to the original interval.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection holds unless the exact joint transport-cut dual yields a strictly smaller envelope and a derived critical shift; this was not established, so the seed is not retained.

seed_details.title: Optimal support complexity of endpoint-attaining categorical SCMs
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Opened R-28 and read Definition 3.1, Theorem 3.2 and its eight-mass construction, and the Conclusion. The proof gives binary witnesses but does not characterize minimum witness support as alphabets grow.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is cycle cancellation in the flow witness followed by a lower-bound family whose observable margins force many distinct response signatures.
seed_details.destination_search: Searched sparse SCM certificates, minimum support response types, PoC extreme points, and transportation-polytope support. Generic basic-feasible-solution bounds exist, but no matched support frontier for this structured completion was located.
seed_details.red_team: Carathéodory immediately supplies the optimal support order.
seed_details.rebuttal: Carathéodory supplies only a generic upper bound; matching structured lower bounds and certificate-preserving compression are not immediate, but the question is secondary to sharpness.

seed_details.title: Sharp conjunction PoC bounds with only selected intervention rows
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Opened arXiv:2505.15274v4 and read the setup requiring the relevant experimental effects, Theorem 2, and Conclusion. The sharp region when some queried intervention rows are absent is not treated by that theorem.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step leaves selected success marginals free and projects the packing and flow inequalities over those nuisance rows before constructing a joint categorical completion.
seed_details.destination_search: Searched missing intervention arms, partial experiments, multivalued PNS bounds, and flow projection. Incomplete-subpopulation work is adjacent but does not give this missing-arm scalar projection.
seed_details.red_team: Optimizing the published formula over missing marginals is automatically sharp.
seed_details.rebuttal: Projection of separately sharp scalar formulas need not preserve a common endpoint witness; a joint completion theorem is still required.

threads: Shu--Wang--Li, arXiv:2505.15274v4, Theorem 2 and Appendix A.1: the exact scalar affine bounds are proved valid; the Introduction at Section 1 and Conclusion at Section 6 leave all-dimensional tightness open.

Xie--Li, R-28, Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2: every-input attainability is proved for binary PNS by an eight-cell active-region construction; the Introduction identifies nonbinary completion as the harder destination.
Koperberg, Statistics \& Probability Letters 209 (2024), Proposition 6: finite coupling with deficiency is equivalent to Hall inequalities, supplying the flow-and-cut technique adapted here.

Rossetto--Antonucci, arXiv:2608.24427, Theorems 2--4 and Section 3 complexity discussion: response-signature linear programs are sharp and SCM-attained, but their general representation does not give this scalar closed form or polynomial witness construction.
literature_map.subsumption_check: No closer source located after exact-title, author-follow-up, conjunction-PNS, max-flow, coupling, and response-signature searches supplies the categorical lifting, the diagonal-deleted residual invariant, or the stated rational certificate bounds.

threads: Cheng--Mao--Pearl--Li, arXiv:2602.17070, Theorems 1--2 and Section 6: unique-active and tied-active asymptotic laws are derived, with multilevel applicability stated, but finite-sample uniform inversion is not supplied.

Horowitz--Lee, Journal of Business \& Economic Statistics 41 (2023), Theorem 2.1 and Conclusion: confidence enlargement for optimization-defined partially identified parameters transfers set containment to finite-sample coverage under its assumptions.
Stoye, Econometrica 77 (2009): confidence intervals are designed to remain valid as the identified interval degenerates, an issue shared by conjunction PoCs.

Kaido--Molinari--Stoye, Econometrica 87 (2019): calibrated projection controls asymptotic coverage uniformly for moment-inequality projections, but does not give the exact block-multinomial finite-sample construction here.
literature_map.subsumption_check: The generic containment argument is known, so novelty is limited to the explicit polynomial positive-part inversion for the sharp all-alphabet PoC endpoint and its zero-cell, tie, and empty-region audit.

threads: Shu--Wang--Li, arXiv:2505.15274v4, Theorems 3--5: closed formulas are given for substitute, replacement, and necessity representatives.
Li--Pearl, AAAI 2024: recursive multivalued PoC bounds cover these families, with many tightness questions unresolved.
Xie--Li, R-28: constructive tightness is confined to binary PNS and does not preserve extra factual slices.
Xie--Li, arXiv:2602.14503: partial-diagram response programs accept extra constraints but do not derive a universal closed sliced-flow theorem.
literature_map.subsumption_check: No closer theorem was found, but feasibility is materially lower because the scalar residual-fill invariant does not survive factual slicing without a new argument.

novelty_justification: The closest published formula is Shu--Wang--Li Theorem 2, which proves soundness and reports low-dimensional linear-program evidence while explicitly leaving all-dimensional tightness open. The closest constructive theorem is Xie--Li Theorem 3.2, restricted to binary PNS and an eight-response-cell partition. The proposed kernel proves the missing every-compatible-input statement for arbitrary finite treatment and outcome alphabets by an exact indicator projection and categorical lifting, intersection packing for the upper endpoint, and a complete bipartite flow with deleted diagonal plus a residual-failure filling invariant for the lower endpoint. Rossetto--Antonucci already supplies generic response-signature LP sharpness and SCM realization, so neither LP existence nor generic endpoint attainability is claimed as new. The strict delta is a compact closed-form proof and polynomial primal--dual certificate system for the specific scalar margin problem. Cheng--Mao--Pearl--Li owns active-set directional inference; the inference rung here is only finite-sample confidence-region inversion.
